frameworks.name: Noora
frameworks.citation: Koegel, L. K., et al. (2025). Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Empathetic Statements in Autistic Adolescents and Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial. Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders.
frameworks.rationale: Noora is text-based by construction so it scores verbal content, not warmth or paraverbals. Designed for and tested with autistic users (38% improvement in empathic responses after 4 weeks).

frameworks.name: MITI 4.2.1
frameworks.citation: Moyers, T. B., Manuel, J. K., & Ernst, D. (2014). Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity Coding Manual 4.2.1. Univ. of New Mexico CASAA.
frameworks.rationale: Operationalizes empathy as reflective listening with simple vs. complex reflections. Behavior-counted, content-based, no tone scoring.

frameworks.name: Thin-slice bias is style-driven, not content-driven
frameworks.citation: Sasson, N. J., Faso, D. J., Nugent, J., Lovell, S., Kennedy, D. P., & Grossman, R. B. (2017). Neurotypical peers are less willing to interact with those with autism based on thin slice judgments. Scientific Reports, 7:40700.
frameworks.rationale: Bias against autistic adults fires within thin slices and is style-driven; when evaluators see only transcripts (no audio/video), the negative bias disappears. Direct empirical justification for never re-introducing style-as-content via 'warmth' criteria.

frameworks.name: Practical empathy is empathy
frameworks.citation: Fletcher-Watson, S., & Bird, G. (2020). Autism and empathy: What are the real links? Autism, 24(1), 3-6. (See also Bird & Cook, 2013, Translational Psychiatry, 3:e285 — alexithymia hypothesis.)
frameworks.rationale: Reduced expressive empathy markers often track alexithymia (a co-occurring trait), not autism per se; affective concern is intact. Score empathic content (acknowledgment, reflection, autonomy-respecting offer), not warmth performance.

frameworks.name: Rapport is a dyad property
frameworks.citation: Crompton, C. J., et al. (2020). Autistic peer-to-peer information transfer is highly effective. Autism, 24(7), 1704-1712. (Companion: Crompton et al., 2020, Frontiers in Psychology 11:586171 — neurotype-matching, not autism, drives rapport.)
frameworks.rationale: Rapport drops only in mixed neurotype dyads; autistic-to-autistic transfer is as efficient as NT-to-NT. 'Felt rapport' is a property of the dyad, not the speaker. Evaluator-LLM proxies for rapport (warmth, charm) must not influence scoring.

0.label: Missing
0.criteria: No reference to coworker's stated state.

2.label: Specific
2.example: Being tired and unable to focus is hard.

0.label: Off-topic / hijacking
0.criteria: Off-topic, dismissive, or makes it about self.
0.example: I'm tired too, let me tell you about my week.

1.label: Tangential pivot
1.criteria: Tangentially related; partial pivot to advice or other topic.

2.label: Stays with experience
2.criteria: Stays with the coworker's experience before anything else.
2.example: Thanks for telling me. That sounds like it's been wearing on you.

2.label: Complex reflection
2.criteria: Names content AND an inferred meaning or impact.
2.example: Sounds like the fatigue is making work harder than usual.

0.label: Leads with judgement
0.criteria: Leads with judgement, advice, or solution.

1.label: Mixed
1.example: That's tough — try going to bed earlier.

2.label: Acknowledges first
2.criteria: Acknowledges first; offers help only as an option.
2.example: That sounds hard. Want to talk about it, or is there something I can take off your plate?

1.label: Open but vague
1.example: Let me know if you need anything.

2.label: Specific autonomy-respecting offer
2.criteria: Specific, low-pressure offer that respects autonomy.
2.example: If you want to share more I'm around. No pressure either way.

strong.label: S1 — low-affect, direct (neurodivergent-friendly)
strong.response: That sounds hard. Tiredness like that makes concentrating really difficult. Let me know if you want me to take anything off your plate.
strong.reasoning: Names state (D1), stays on-topic (D2), complex reflection naming impact (D3), no advice (D4), specific autonomy-respecting offer (D5). No warmth performance required.

strong.label: S2 — matter-of-fact, brief
strong.response: Thanks for telling me. Tired and unfocused is a rough combo.
strong.reasoning: Direct, factual acknowledgement with a complex reflection (D3) — flat affect is fine.

strong.label: S3 — reflective, longer
strong.response: Sounds like it's been building up and the focus part is the worst of it. I appreciate you saying something.
strong.reasoning: Strong complex reflection inferring a pattern (D3) without performing warmth.

weak.label: W1 — fixing first
weak.response: You should try melatonin and cut out caffeine after 2pm.
weak.reasoning: Skips D1 acknowledgement; leads with fixing (D4 fail).

weak.label: W2 — hijacking
weak.response: Ugh, I'm exhausted too — last night was brutal for me.
weak.reasoning: Hijacks the topic (D2 fail); no acknowledgement of their state (D1 fail).

weak.label: W3 — minimal
weak.reasoning: No acknowledgement, no reflection, no offer.

do_not_score: Tone, warmth, or affect — flat or matter-of-fact delivery scores equally to expressive delivery

Emotional mirroring or 'feeling-with' performance — practical empathy is empathy (Bird & Cook 2013; Fletcher-Watson & Bird 2020). Affective concern can be expressed through acknowledgment + low-pressure offer without affective performance
Eye contact, facial expression, body language — out of scope for text rubric
Paraverbal cues — pace, prosody, sighs, aw's
Politeness softeners — 'oh no', 'aww', 'I'm so sorry' are optional, not required

Length or verbosity — concise responses can score 10/10. Long, deeply attentive on-topic responses (monotropism: Murray et al. 2005; Garau et al. 2023) ALSO score 10/10. Length is not a signal in either direction

Tangential thinking when the response ultimately lands D1+D3 — associative thought is a valid path (Kucyi et al. 2025; Bozhilova et al. 2018). Score whether the response lands on the rubric, not whether it goes straight there
Self-disclosure of similar feelings — neither required nor rewarded; can hurt D2 if it hijacks
Idiomatic neurotypical phrasing — direct literal language is fully acceptable
Absence of warmth tokens (exclamation points, 'aww', emoji, intensifiers) — neutral, not negative
'Rapport', 'connection', or 'felt warmth' between user and avatar — these are dyad properties (Crompton et al. 2020a/b), not user performance
evaluator_directive: If the LLM evaluator finds itself wanting to deduct points for sounding cold, not warm enough, too blunt, too brief, too long, or because the partner 'might find this hard to read' — it must not. Re-score on content only. The double empathy literature (Milton 2012; Crompton et al. 2020a/b) is unambiguous: communicative breakdown in mixed-neurotype interaction is bidirectional, not a one-way deficit. Practical-support offers ('want me to take the 3pm meeting?') count fully toward D5 — practical empathy is empathy (Fletcher-Watson & Bird 2020). A brief, direct, low-affect response that hits D1+D3+D4 scores 6+/10 with zero warmth performance.
attribution: Workplace empathy rubric grounded in the Stanford HAI Noora framework (Koegel et al., 2025, J. Autism Dev. Disord., doi:10.1007/s10803-025-06734-x), the MITI 4.2.1 reflective-listening coding system (Moyers, Manuel & Ernst, 2014), the double empathy literature (Milton 2012; Crompton et al. 2020a/b), and Sasson et al. 2017 (Sci. Rep.) which empirically established that bias against autistic adults is style-driven and disappears in transcript-only evaluation — direct justification for ScenarioLab's text-rubric surface.
